evals.prompt: I moved from India to Canada in 2019 and visit once or twice a year. I sold some mutual funds in FY 2025-26. Do I need to file an Indian return, and which form?
evals.expected_output: Pins the year, determines residential status from the person's trip estimates, and chooses the ITR form and regime.
expectations: States both FY 2025-26 and AY 2026-27 and checks the person means that year
Asks for approximate India trips and lengths per year instead of searching the mailbox for travel evidence
Uses scripts/residency_days.py or the residency rules to reach a status
Reaches Non-Resident given the facts, and explains the deciding test
Says a non-resident cannot use ITR-1 and points to ITR-2 for capital gains
Notes that non-residents get no 87A rebate

evals.prompt: I missed the 31 July deadline for my ITR. What are my options now and what will it cost?
evals.expected_output: The belated-return route and its costs, the updated-return fallback, quantified with the calculator.
expectations: Checks whether the return is actually late for the person's form
Explains a belated return under section 139(4) is possible until 31 December of the AY
States the 234F fee (₹5,000, or ₹1,000 if total income is up to ₹5 lakh)
Explains 234A interest and, if relevant, 234B/234C
Says a belated return is locked into the new regime
Mentions ITR-U as the later fallback and that it cannot claim a refund
Quantifies the cost with scripts/india_tax_calc.py

evals.prompt: The Schedule 112A CSV upload on the e-filing portal keeps failing with common.errors.csv_row_skip. Here are my fund sales.
evals.expected_output: A complete, ready-to-upload 112A file in the format the portal accepts, with instructions on existing rows.
expectations: Explains post-31 Jan 2018 holdings go in one consolidated row (ISIN INNOTREQUIRD, name CONSOLIDATED)
Uses whole rupees
Keeps separate rows for pre-Feb-2018 holdings with grandfathered cost
Delivers the complete file, not a partial patch
Says which existing rows to delete before uploading
Uses scripts/schedule_112a_helper.py

evals.prompt: I'm in the UK. When I add my tax challan on the portal it says 'Date of Deposit cannot be more than System Date'. I paid it last night.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the time-zone clash and gives the safe fix without altering the challan.
expectations: Identifies the clash between a payment after midnight IST and a session still on the previous date
Says never to change the challan date
Gives the fixes: start a new session, wait, or switch the computer to IST

evals.prompt: I'm an NRI and my only Indian income is about ₹3 lakh of equity fund gains plus some fixed-deposit interest. Why is the portal showing so much tax? Did I make a mistake?
evals.expected_output: Explains the non-resident rules that produce the tax, and checks fund classification, instead of assuming a filing error.
expectations: Explains that a non-resident's unused basic exemption cannot absorb special-rate capital gains
Explains non-residents get no 87A rebate
Applies the ₹1.25 lakh 112A exemption only to equity-oriented gains
Checks whether any funds are international or non-equity, taxed under section 112 without the exemption
Checks the portal's figure against its own computation and says plainly whether there is an error

evals.prompt: I need my mutual fund capital gains statement for FY 2025-26 to file. Where do I get it?
evals.expected_output: Points to MF Central first, with the broker Tax P&L and AIS as cross-checks, not an email hunt.
expectations: Recommends MF Central first (PAN plus OTP, one statement covering CAMS and KFintech funds)
Mentions the broker's Tax P&L for directly held shares
Mentions reconciling against AIS
Does not start by searching the person's email for statements
Does not send the person to CAMS and KFintech separately as the first step
